title: The Refund Owed When Waiver Coverage on an Auto Loan Is Closed Out
content:
The refund owed on the waiver coverage financed with a loan of the Auto Loans line, when that coverage is closed out, is the unearned part of the charge financed at funding, less the cancellation fee. It is entered against the loan rather than paid out to the borrower, so the loan's unpaid principal falls by it.

The unearned part is the refundable share of the charge financed at funding, multiplied by the months remaining and divided by the term the loan was written for, and the cancellation fee is deducted from it once it is settled. No refund is entered where that figure comes to nothing or less.

The refundable share is 90 percent of the charge financed at funding. The months remaining are the term less the whole months since funding. The unearned part is measured on the whole months remaining over the term. The cancellation fee is the one the product publishes. The refund is rounded half-up to the cent.

## A refund worked out on hypothetical readings

| Reading | Value |
|---|---|
| Charge financed at funding | 695.00 USD |
| Term the loan was written for | 60 months |
| Whole months since funding | 18 |
| Cancellation fee the product publishes | 50.00 USD |

The months remaining are 60 less 18, which is 42.

The refundable share of the charge financed at funding is 90 percent of 695.00, which is 625.50.

The unearned part is 625.50 multiplied by 42 and divided by 60, which is 437.85.

The cancellation fee is deducted from that, leaving 387.85. Rounded half-up to the cent, the refund entered against the loan is 387.85 USD, and the loan's unpaid principal falls by that sum.

## When no refund is entered

Were the same loan 58 whole months old, the months remaining would be 2, the unearned part would be 625.50 multiplied by 2 and divided by 60, which is 20.85, and deducting the cancellation fee would leave a figure below nothing. No refund is entered in that case.
